header: IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT, LAHORE
body: Date of hearing: 22.04.2025 Petitioner by: M/s Uzman Umar Khokhar and Ch.
Ahsan Ahmad Gujjar, Advocates State by: Mr. Amjad Javed, Deputy Prosecutor General.

TANVEER AHMAD SHEIKH, J: Petitioner Sheikh Irfan Ahmad/surety has assailed the orders dated 31.05.2016 and 06.04.2017, passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore, whereby he was burdened with an amount of Rs.50,000/under Section 514 of Cr.P.C. and District Collector, Lahore was directed to proceed further for the recovery of the amount.

2. According to actual and factual background one Sheikh Kamran Ahmad (real brother of petitioner) was allowed ad-interim pre-arrest bail being accused of case F.I.R. No.347/2014, for offences under Sections 420,467, 468 and 471 PPC of Police Station Old Anarkali, Lahore, through order dated 08.09.2014 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore. Petitioner stood surety for his brother, having submitted bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- . Said accused absented himself from the court on 12.11.2014, resulting into the dismissal of pre-arrest bail petition in default. Respondent No.2 (Amjad Ali Sherazi), complainant of above case, moved an application before the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, for initiation of proceedings under Section 514 of Cr.P.C. against the present petitioner (surety). The learned court, after seeking reply from petitioner/surety, passed an order dated 31.05.2016 (impugned order), directing the initiation of above proceedings against the petitioner/surety. Respondent No.2 (complainant of the F.I.R.) moved another application to the court of learned Addiotional Sessions Judge, with the prayer that matter be referred to Revenue Department for the recovery of above amount of Rs.50,000/-, which was accepted and District Collector, Lahore was ordered to recover the above amount from present petitioner/surety vide order 06.04.2017 (impugned order).

3. Learned counsel for petitioner, at the very outset, raised the objection that it was within the sole discretion of the learned court of Additional Sessions Judge to initiate the above proceedings or not and an application on behalf of complainant of F.I.R. was not competent in this regard, because submission of the surety bond and thereafter violation of the same was a matter between court and surety/accused.

4. The language used in Section 514 of Cr.P.C. empowers the court to call upon a person bound by such bond to pay the penalty to show cause why it should not be paid, after it is proved to the satisfaction of the court that the bail bond was forfeited. Said power may be exercised by the court of his own or on the application of any concerned person. Moving of the application to the court by complainant of F.I.R. does not bind the court to initiate the proceedings at all cost. Moving of the application by complainant was amount to bring the matter into the knowledge of the court. The court may initiate the proceedings or may decline the application in its discretion. Law does not put any embargo upon the complainant of F.I.R. from moving such like application, as such the application was competent in my humble view.

5. In the case in hand, when the order dated 31.05.2016 was passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore, directing the initiation of proceedings under Section 514 of Cr.P.C. but he failed to pass an order for the forfeiture of the surety bond, which was mandatory and a condition precedent in the light of the dictums laid down by Honourable Superior Courts in plethora of judgments. So much so, when he passed second order dated 06.04.2017 directing the District Collector, Lahore for the recovery of the amount of surety bond, he did not bother to pass any such order for the forfeiture of surety bond. He also did not issue any notice to the petitioner to provide him an opportunity to submit reply and advance arguments, while passing order dated 06.04.2017. He was not allowed to justify his position.

6. The learned Additional Sessions Judge was required to forfeit the surety bond first and then to issue notice to the petitioner providing him opportunity to show sufficient casue or to pay the penalty under sub section 2 of Section 514 of Cr.P.C. before passing any order for the attachment of his movable property. If any reference in this regard is required, that can be had from ‘Muhammad Rafique Versus The State’ (PLD 2009 Lahore 132) and ‘Mukhtar Ali Versus The State and others’ (1991 P Cr.LJ 1625 Lahore).
Said procedure was not adopted by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore. Above illegality committed by him was not cureable.

7. File speaks that in the matter in hand, the accused after absenting from the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore, did not obtain ad-interim pre-arrest bail again, because criminal case was recommended for cancellation, as such there was neither any occasion for the accused to surrender himself before the court, nor for the petitioner/surety to produce him before the court. His responsibility stood absorbed. Above fact was not adhere to by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore, as such the impugned orders being improper were also liable to be set aside on that score alone.

8. So far as other merits of the case are concerned, I am of the confirmed view that the learned court while imposing penalty upon surety should take into consideration following aspects:i. Circumstances under which the bail bond was submitted by surety.
ii. Relationship of surety, if any, with the accused. iii. Whether surety submitted bail bond out of benevolence and on humanitarian/compassionate ground, or he obtained any monetary gain.
iv. Financial/social status of surety as well as that of the accused.
v. Nature/gravity of the offence and social impact thereof, for which the bail bond was submitted.
vi. Amount of the bond, whether it commensurate with the nature and gravity of the offence.
vii. Circumstances under which accused disappeared, or absconded, or violated the terms and conditions of bail bond.
viii. Length of the absence or abscondence of accused and other allied/ancillary circumstances.

9. In the case in hand, petitioner stood surety not for a stranger, but for a person/accused, who happened to be his real brother, as such there was nothing to draw an inference to the effect that he obtained any monetary benefit from the accused for submission of bail bond. Accused, after dismissal of his petition for pre-arrest bail for non-prosecution, was not supposed to reappear before the court for obtaining ad-interim pre-arrest bail again, because the criminal case against him was recommended for cancellation. There was no absence or absconscion on the part of accused. He remained available throughout. He is also in attendance today alongwith his brother/petitioner.

10. I feel no hasitation in holding that impugned orders passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, were in flagrant violation of the procedure laid down by law and endorsed by Honourable Superior Courts. Even otherwise, the same were not found to have been passed keeping in view the attending circumstances, which rendered the orders improper and illegal and liable to be set aside.
11. Revision accepted.
(TANVEER AHMAD SHEIKH)
JUDGE Approved for reporting.
JUDGE *Shahzad Ahmad Nasir*
